name: Canon FL 400 mm f/ 5.6
note: no FL 400mm f/5.6 was ever made. The 1971 Focusing-Unit super-telephoto is f/4.5 (Wikipedia FL table lists 400/4.5, 600/5.6, 800/8, 1200/11; no f/5.6 400 in any source list). The correctly-named record is curated in the forge; this fold redirects the shipped id.

name: Canon FL 300 mm f/ 2.5 S.S.C. florite

note: guard row for the aperture-typo spelling, in case a source ever emits it. Primary fold is the row below.

name: Canon FL 300 mm f/ 2.8 S.S.C. florite
merge_into: Canon FL 300 mm f/ 2.8 S.S.C. Fluorite
note: 'florite' is a source typo for Fluorite (the CaF2 element that made this 1974 lens famous). Renaming re-keys the id, so the correct spelling is curated in the forge and this fold redirects the shipped id.

name: Canon FL M 50 mm f/ 3.5
note: same lens — the 1965 FL Macro 50mm; 'FL-M' is Canon's designation prefix for it, not a second product. Both records carried 1965 and identical optics.

name: Canon FD 85 mm f/ 1.2 SSC Aspherical
merge_into: Canon FD 85 mm f/ 1.2 S.S.C. Aspherical
note: punctuation twins — the same 1976-1980 lens spelled with and without the dots. Identical years and specs on both records.

name: Canon FD 70-210 mm f/ 4
note: the 70-210mm f/4 existed only in the New FD generation (1980) — there was no breech-lock version, so the FD-named record is the same lens under the seller's spelling. The fold keeps the seller name resolving via redirect + alias.

name: Canon Zoom Lens FD 35-70mm 1:4 AF
merge_into: Canon AF Zoom FD 35-70 mm f/ 4
note: the same 1981 autofocus New FD 35-70mm f/4 AF — one record named off the barrel engraving ('1:4'), one off the catalog name. One lens, one record.

name: Canon FDn 50 mm f/ 3.5 Macro
note: the record carried 1973 — the breech-lock FD 50/3.5 Macro S.S.C.'s year. The New FD version this record names arrived June 1979 (Canon Camera Museum). The breech version now has its own curated record with the 1973 date.
